BURHAN:v2p129/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p129/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p129/r3.claim: The hadith that actions depend on intentions has an explicit Quranic basis in the contrast between seeking the immediate world and the Hereafter, and in accountability for what hearts intend and oaths they bind.
BURHAN:v2p129/r3.anchor: ثم بدأ رضى الله عنه بحديث ( إنما الأعمال بالنيات ) وقال موضعه نصافي قوله تعالى

DURR-FULL:v4p405/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p405/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p405/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the desired life as its reward and adornment as its wealth; God fully grants health, family joy, money, and children, a rule he says was abrogated by 17:18.
DURR-FULL:v4p405/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما {من كان يريد الحياة الدنيا} أي ثوابها {وزينتها} مالها

STUDYQURAN:17:intro/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:intro/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:17:intro/r6.claim: Its themes include God's power over nature and repeated warnings of punishment on earth or in the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:17:intro/r6.anchor: references to God’s Power over the natural world (vv. 66–70), repeated warnings to human beings about the coming of Divine Punishment

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Section III invites Jews and Quraysh to the Qur’an's natural straight path, contrasts the fates of acceptance and rejection, rebukes those blind to signs who demand punishment, and alludes to God's practice of punishing nations.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: both the Jews and the Idolaters of the Quraysh are invited to profess faith in the Qur’ ān

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Al-‘ājilah contrasts with the Hereafter and means this world and its immediate gains.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: is used in contrast to the hereafter and hence refers to this world and to is immediate gains

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Islahi flags God's choosing who receives immediate worldly benefits and in what quantity as central to His practice of giving respite; this extract cuts off before his explanation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: need to be specially kept in mind

BURSEVI:v5p110/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p110/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p110/r1.claim: The worldly-minded do deeds solely for immediate life: disbelievers, sinners, hypocrites, ostentatious worshippers, and migrants or fighters seeking only gain or fame.
BURSEVI:v5p110/r1.anchor: والمهاجر للدنيا والمجاهد لمحض الغنيمة والذكر

BURSEVI:v5p110/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p110/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p110/r2.claim: God grants such a person only what He wills, not everything desired, because wisdom does not require every seeker to obtain every wish.
BURSEVI:v5p110/r2.anchor: تعجيله له من نعيمها لا كل ما يريد فإن الحكمة لا تقتضي وصول كل واحد إلى جميع ما يهواه

BURSEVI:v5p110/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p110/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p110/r3.claim: People are tested differently: some seek without receiving, some receive what they seek now or later, and some receive without seeking.
BURSEVI:v5p110/r3.anchor: وبعضهم لا يبتلى بالطلب بل يصل إليه الفيض بلا طلب

BURSEVI:v5p110/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p110/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p110/r4.claim: The phrase لمن نريد is a partitive substitute for the pronoun in له, since that pronoun refers to a collective relative and only some are granted what God chooses.
BURSEVI:v5p110/r4.anchor: بدل البعض فإنه راجع إلى الموصول المنبىء عن الكثرة

BURSEVI:v5p110/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p110/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p110/r5.claim: Instead of the accelerated worldly gift, the person enters Hell blameworthy and expelled from divine mercy; madhmum means blamed and madhur means driven away.
BURSEVI:v5p110/r5.anchor: مطرودا من رحمة الله تعالى فإن الدحر الطرد والإبعاد

ALUSI-FULL:v15p45#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p45#2/r1.speaker: الضحاك
ALUSI-FULL:v15p45#2/r1.claim: The one who desires the immediate world does so through deeds and wants it alone, not the afterlife; Alusi cites al-Dahhak through Ibn Abi Hatim.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p45#2/r1.anchor: أي بعلمه كما أخرجه ابن أبي حاتم عن الضحاك ( العاجلة ( فقط من غير أن يريد معها الآخرة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p45#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p45#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p45#2/r2.claim: The added كان conveys continued or exclusive desire; the alternative that the person may desire both worlds does not fit the passage's division, and defining desire as inward resolve is insufficient.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p45#2/r2.anchor: كما ينبيء عنه الاستمرار المستفاد من زيادة ( كان ) هنا مع الاقتصار على مطلق الإرادة في قسيمه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p45#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p45#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p45#2/r3.claim: The immediate world means worldly life and its many aims, as in verses about seeking worldly harvest, its adornments, or its reward.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p45#2/r3.anchor: والمراد بالعاجلة الدار الدنيا كما روى الضحاك أيضا وبإرادتها إرادة ما فيها من فنون مطالبها

ALUSI-FULL:v15p45#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p45#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p45#2/r4.claim: Some interpret the immediate world specifically as this short life, supported by another verse about worldly life and its adornment; Alusi prefers the broader world-and-its-aims sense as more fitting here.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p45#2/r4.anchor: وجوز أن يراد الحياة العاجلة كقوله تعالى : ( من كان يريد الحياة الدنيا وزينتها ) ورجح الأول

ALUSI-FULL:v15p45#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p45#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p45#2/r5.claim: God hastens only some of the worldly enjoyment He chooses to the recipient, not everything each person wants.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p45#2/r5.anchor: ما نشاء ( أي ما نشاء تعجيله له من نعيمها لا كل ما يريد

ALUSI-FULL:v15p45#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p45#2/r6.speaker: أبو إسحاق الفزاري
ALUSI-FULL:v15p45#2/r6.claim: Abu Ishaq al-Fazari reads لمن نريد as those God wants to destroy, but Alusi says the wording does not support that gloss.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p45#2/r6.anchor: وقال أبو إسحق الفزاري : أي لمن نريد هلكته ولا يدل عليه لفظ في الآية

ALUSI-FULL:v15p45#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p45#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p45#2/r7.claim: The phrase لمن نريد can be parsed as a replacement for له or for its pronoun, with an understood recipient and a pronoun referring to the relative or conditional person.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p45#2/r7.anchor: والجار والمجرور بدل من الجار والمجرور السابق أعني له فلا يحتاج إلى رابط

ALUSI-FULL:v15p45#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p45#2/r8.speaker: نافع
ALUSI-FULL:v15p45#2/r8.claim: Nafi reads يشاء with a yā; the pronoun may refer to God, matching the other reading, or to the recipient, particularly someone God lets succeed as a form of enticement.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p45#2/r8.anchor: وعن نافع أنه قرأ ( ما يشاء ) بالياء فقيل الضمير فيه لله تعالى فيتطابق القراءتان

ALUSI-FULL:v15p45#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p45#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p45#2/r9.claim: Divine wisdom does not grant every seeker every wish or let any recipient exhaust all they desire; the contrast between مشيئة and إرادة may simply vary expression.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p45#2/r9.anchor: لما أن الحكمة التي يدور عليها فلك التكوين ولا تقتضي وصول كل طالب إلى مرامه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p46/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p46/r1.speaker: الخليل
ALUSI-FULL:v15p46/r1.claim: Al-Khalil explains يصلاها as enduring the heat of Hell; another gloss is entering it.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p46/r1.anchor: يقاسي حرها كما قال الخليل أو يدخلها كما قيل

ALUSI-FULL:v15p46/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p46/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v15p46/r2.claim: Abu al-Baqa treats يصلاها as a circumstantial clause modifying the pronoun in له; Abu Hayyan instead makes it a circumstance of Hell, the first object of جعلنا.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p46/r2.anchor: والجملة كما قال أبو البقاء حال من الهاء في ( له ) وقال أبو حيان : إنها حال من ( جهنم )

ALUSI-FULL:v15p46/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p46/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p46/r3.claim: Alusi rejects the need to posit an omitted second object such as destination or recompense after جعلنا.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p46/r3.anchor: وجوز أن تكون الجملة مستأنفة وقال صاحب الغينان : مفعول جعلنا الثاني محذوف

ALUSI-FULL:v15p46/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p46/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p46/r4.claim: مذموما describes the person as blameworthy, while مدحورا means expelled and distanced from God's mercy.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p46/r4.anchor: حال من فاعل يصلى وهو من الذم ضد المدح

ALUSI-FULL:v15p46/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p46/r5.speaker: الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p46/r5.claim: Al-Razi defines punishment as lasting harm joined to humiliation and without benefit; the verse's Hell and banishment therefore imply enduring punishment with no relief.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p46/r5.anchor: إن العقاب عبارة عن مضرة مقرونة بالإهانة والذم بشرط أن تكون دائمة وخالية عن المنفعة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p46/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p46/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p46/r6.claim: Because the verse implies everlasting Hell, Alusi says its subject must be an unbeliever.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p46/r6.anchor: ظاهر في أن الآية تدل على الخلود وحينئذ يتعين عندنا أن يكون ذلك المريد من الكفرة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p46/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p46/r7.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v15p46/r7.claim: Abu Hayyan takes the person as an unbeliever who prefers the world to the afterlife; he also reports a reading that includes hypocrites, show-offs, and people seeking spoils or worldly migration.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p46/r7.anchor: ومعنى إرادتها إيثارها على الآخرة ولابد من تقدير محذوف دل عليه المقابل

ALUSI-FULL:v15p46/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p46/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p46/r8.claim: Including sinful believers, worldly migrants, or fighters seeking spoils cannot imply eternal Hell on Alusi's theology; instead banishment can describe a believer while in Hell, as well as an unbeliever forever.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p46/r8.anchor: إدراج الفاسق والمهاجر للدنيا والمجاهد للغنيمة إذا كان مؤمنا في التمثيل على القول بدلالة الآية على الخلود

ALUSI-FULL:v15p47/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p47/r1.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p47/r1.claim: Some claim the verse was revealed about a hypocrite who joins Muslim campaigns for spoils rather than religious reward.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p47/r1.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أن المريد هو المنافق الذي يغزو مع المسلمين للغنيمة لا للثواب فإن الآية نزلت فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p47/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p47/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p47/r2.claim: Alusi rejects that occasion because the sura is Meccan and this verse is not among its exceptions; in any event, general wording governs beyond a specific occasion.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p47/r2.anchor: وفيه أنه يأبى ذلك ما سبق من أن السورة مكية غير آيات معينة ليست هذه منها على أن العبرة بعموم اللفظ

ALUSI-FULL:v15p52/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p52/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p52/r3.claim: The immediate-world seeker represents a turbid spiritual disposition overwhelmed by desire and natural impulses.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p84/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p84/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p84/r6.claim: Worldly seekers receive only what God wills, whether expansion, restriction, or destruction; afterward they enter Hell blamed and banished.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p84/r6.anchor: {عجلنا له فيها ما نشاء} من البسط والتقتير {لمن نريد} أن نفعل به ذلك أو إهلاكه {ثم جعلنا له} في الآخرة {جهنم يصلاها} يدخل نارها

QASHANI:17:18-21/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:17:18-21/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:17:18-21/r1.claim: The worldly seeker has clouded readiness and dominant appetite; God hastens only the share decreed for whomever He wills, since desire alone cannot secure more than the allotment in the Preserved Tablet.
QASHANI:17:18-21/r1.anchor: من النصيب في اللوح ولذلك قيده بالمشيئة

QASHANI:17:18-21/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:17:18-21/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:17:18-21/r2.claim: Hell is the dark well of nature toward which the seeker inclines: its fire is deprivation, its verdict is blame among both worlds, and its state is expulsion from mercy.
QASHANI:17:18-21/r2.anchor: قعر بئر الطبيعة الظلمانية لانجذابه بإرادته إلى الجهة السفلية

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:18/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:18/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:18/r1.claim: The person seeking the immediate life has made it his sole concern.

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:18/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:18/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:18/r2.claim: Worldly grant is restricted by God’s will and choice, since no one receives every wish or all that they desire; this teaches that achievement and concern are gifts.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:18/r2.anchor: لا يجد كل متمن ما يتمناه، ولا كل واجد

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:18/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:18/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:18/r3.claim: In the phrase “and for whom We will,” the prepositional phrase substitutes for “to him” as a partitive apposition.

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:18/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:18/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:18/r4.claim: A reading has “what He wills,” with the pronoun referring to God so it agrees with the common reading.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:18/r4.anchor: يشاء» والضمير فيه لله تعالى حتى يطابق المشهورة

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:18/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:18/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:18/r5.claim: Another explanation takes “for whom” as a restriction to the person God specifically wills to grant.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:18/r5.anchor: فيكون مخصوصا بمن أراد الله تعالى به ذلك.

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:18/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:18/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:18/r6.claim: One reported interpretation applies the verse to hypocrites who joined Muslims in raids for a share of the spoils, not religious purpose.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:18/r6.anchor: وقيل الآية في المنافقين كانوا يراءون المسلمين ويغزون معهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:18/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:18/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:18/r7.claim: The worldly seeker is cast into Hell, disgraced and driven away from God’s mercy.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p371/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p371/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p371/r1.claim: God treats people according to His knowledge of their inner good and evil; attachment to leadership, wealth, and pleasure can prevent obedience to messengers.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p371/r1.anchor: يعاملهم على حسب علمه على وجه معرف بعلمه بجميع طوياتهم من خير وشر

BIQAI-FULL:v4p371/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p371/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p371/r2.claim: A person seeking only the immediate world receives some, not all, of what God wills for selected people; the outcome depends on divine power rather than the seeker's strength.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p371/r2.anchor: مما يريده لا جميع ما يريده ؛ ثم أبدل من ( له ) قوله تعالى

BIQAI-FULL:v4p371/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p371/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p371/r3.claim: God grants worldly benefit only to those He wills, showing the outcome depends on Him rather than everyone who seeks it.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p371/r3.anchor: أي لا لكل من أراد ذلك , تنبيها على أن ذلك بقوتنا لا بقوة ذلك المريد

BIQAI-FULL:v4p371/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p371/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p371/r4.claim: The worldly-only seeker ultimately enters Hell disgraced and driven away; denial brings loss in both lives, while partial worldly success still leaves unmet wishes and afterlife punishment.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p371/r4.anchor: أي مفعولا به الذم , وهو ضد المدح

BIQAI-FULL:v4p371/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p371/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p371/r5.claim: If denied worldly wishes the seeker suffers both losses; if granted something, the person still fails to receive everything desired and faces next-life punishment.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p371/r5.anchor: فقل الدنيا وعذاب الآخرة , وإن أعطى فهو لا يعطي كل ما يريد

DURR-FULL:v5p254/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p254/r8.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v5p254/r8.claim: The seeker of the immediate world is one who does deeds intending worldly gain; God hastens what He wills for whom He wills.
DURR-FULL:v5p254/r8.anchor: عن الضحاك رضي الله عنه في قوله: {من كان يريد العاجلة} قال: من كان يريد بعمله الدنيا

DURR-FULL:v5p254/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p254/r9.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p254/r9.claim: The immediate-world seeker makes it his concern, desire, request, and intention; God gives what He wills, then consigns him to Hell, disgraced under divine wrath and expelled into punishment.
DURR-FULL:v5p254/r9.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله: {من كان يريد العاجلة} قال: من كانت همه ورغبته وطلبته ونيته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p58#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p58#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p58#2/r2.claim: The worldly-minded group wants only this life, serving its desires because it sees no life after death.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p58#2/r2.anchor: قسم لم يرد إلا الدنيا فكانت أعماله لمرضاة شهواته معتقدا أن الدنيا هي قصارى مراتع النفوس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p58#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p58#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p58#2/r4.claim: The contrast between the two sentences supplies an added, contextual restriction: the first person wants the immediate world alone.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p58#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p58#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p58#2/r5.claim: Al-ājilah is an adjective whose omitted noun is life, understood from context and parallel wording.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p58#2/r5.anchor: صفة موصوف محذوف يعلم من السياق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p60/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p60/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p60/r1.claim: The present tense depicts renewed worldly desire, while the past tense and omitted kāna make afterlife desire sound settled and especially worthy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p60/r1.anchor: والاختلاف بين جملة من كان يريد العاجلة } وجملة { ومن أراد الآخرة } بجعل الفعل مضارعا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p446/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p446/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p446/r1.claim: The warning concerns one who wants only worldly life and believes in no afterlife; God grants only what He wills, then consigns all such unbelievers to Hell.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p446/r1.anchor: ولا يعتقد غيرها ولا يؤمن بآخرة فهو يفرغ أمله ومعتقده للدنيا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p446/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p446/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p446/r2.claim: On the reading with “We will,” the object may be what the seeker or God wishes; “for whom We will” qualifies both readings.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p446/r2.anchor: ما يشاء هذا المريد أو ما يشاء الله على قراءة من قرأ «نشاء» بالنون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p446/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p446/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق الفزاري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p446/r3.claim: Abū Isḥāq al-Fazārī interprets “for whom We will” as “for one whose destruction We intend.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p446/r3.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق الفزاري المعنى لمن نريد هلكته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p446/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p446/r4.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p446/r4.claim: Most read nashāʾ with nūn; Nāfiʿ also transmits yashāʾ with yāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p446/r4.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: «نشاء» بالنون، وقرأ نافع أيضا «يشاء» بالياء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p446/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p446/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p446/r5.claim: Madḥūr means disgraced, expelled, humiliated, and subject to displeasure.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p446/r5.anchor: و «المدحور» المهان المبعد المذلل المسخوط عليه

SULAMI:v1p384#5/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p384#5/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p384#5/r1.claim: Al-Wasiti links renouncing the world with witnessing the afterlife, and says witnessing divine support erases self-regard while contemplating God's attributes makes servant attributes fall away.
SULAMI:v1p384#5/r1.anchor: قال الواسطي : في ترك الدنيا مشاهدة الآخرة ، وفي مشاهدة الآخرة رفض الدنيا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p20#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p20#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p20#2/r1.claim: The one seeking the immediate world means a person whose deeds are aimed at worldly life; an adjective is used in place of the noun.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p20#2/r1.anchor: يعني من كان يريد بعمله الدنيا فعبر بالنعت عن الاسم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p20#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p20#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p20#2/r2.claim: The worldly provision hastened to such a person is explained either as worldly goods or as expansion and restriction of provision.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p20#2/r2.anchor: عجلنا له فيها ما نشاء من عرض الدنيا وقيل من البسط والتقتير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p20#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p20#2/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق الفزاري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p20#2/r3.claim: One interpretation of those chosen to receive hastened provision is that God intends their destruction.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p20#2/r3.anchor: لمن نريد هلكته قاله أبو اسحاق الفزاري

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p20#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p20#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p20#2/r4.claim: Another interpretation is that God intends to hasten something for that person.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p20#2/r4.anchor: لمن نريد ان نعجل له شيئا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p20#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p20#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p20#2/r5.claim: The passage rebukes people who work for worldly life: they obtain only what was allotted to them, then enter Hell in the afterlife.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p20#2/r5.anchor: ذم لمن اراد بعمله الدنيا وبيان انه لا ينال مع ما يقصده منها الا ما قدر له

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p20#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p20#2/r6.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p20#2/r6.claim: Ibn Jarīr says this verse concerns those who do not believe in resurrection.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p20#2/r6.anchor: وقال ابن جرير هذه الاية لمن لا يوقن بالمعاد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p62#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p62#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p62#2/r1.claim: Not everyone who seeks worldly pleasure receives it; God grants only what He wills to whom He wills, qualifying other verses that state the promise more generally.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p62#2/r1.anchor: ما كل من طلب الدنيا وما فيها من النعيم يحصل له، بل إنما يحصل لمن أراد الله ما يشاء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p62#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p62#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p62#2/r2.claim: The worldly seeker who is assigned Hell enters it engulfed on every side, blamed for choosing the fleeting over the lasting and cast away in humiliation.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p62#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p62#2/r3.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p62#2/r3.claim: A report from ʿAisha calls this world the home of one without a home and the wealth of one without wealth, gathered by one lacking reason.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p62#2/r3.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "الدنيا دار من لا دار له، ومال من لا مال له

JISHUMI:v6p4177/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4177/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4177/r2.claim: “Condemned, expelled” is an adverbial state, while “knowing, seeing” is an accusative of specification or means “from one who knows.”
JISHUMI:v6p4177/r2.anchor: (مذموما مدحورا) نصب على الحال، وقوله: (خبيرا بصيرا) نصب على التمييز،

JISHUMI:v6p4177/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4177/r3.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v6p4177/r3.claim: The promise about worldly seekers was revealed about emigrants seeking booty rather than God's reward.
JISHUMI:v6p4177/r3.anchor: قيل: نزل قوله: (من كان يريد العاجلة) الآيات في قوم من المهاجرين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r1.claim: Those whose sole aim is this world, such as unbelievers and many sinners, receive only what God wills for whomever He chooses; both the grant and its recipient are restricted by divine choice.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r1.anchor: من كانت العاجلة همه ولم يرد غيرها كالكفرة وأكثر الفسقة ، تفضلنا عليه من منافعها بما نشاء لمن نريد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r2.claim: Many people do not receive all they seek, while others are denied even the portion they desire, leaving them poor in both worlds.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r2.anchor: ترى كثيرا من هؤلاء يتمنون ما يتمنون ولا يعطون إلا بعضا منه وكثيرا منهم يتمنون ذلك البعض وقد حرموه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r4.claim: The phrase for whom We will is an appositional subset of the preceding recipient, since the pronoun refers to people collectively.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r4.anchor: وقوله { لمن نريد } بدل من له ، وهو بدل البعض من الكل : لأن الضمير يرجع إلى ( من ) وهو في معنى الكثرة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r5.claim: A reading has yashāʾ; if the pronoun refers to God, it has the same sense as the standard reading.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r5.anchor: وقرىء : ( يشاء ) وقيل : الضمير لله تعالى ، فلا فرق إذا بين القراءتين في المعنى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r6.claim: Alternatively the pronoun may refer to the servant, meaning the person receives the worldly things he wishes for, though God intends that grant for one of the many.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r6.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون للعبد ، على أن للعبد ما يشاء من الدنيا . وأن ذلك لواحد من الدهماء يريد به الله ذلك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r7.claim: Another kind of worldly seeker performs afterlife deeds for worldly ends: hypocrisy, showing off, migration for gain or marriage, and fighting for spoils or fame.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r7.anchor: هو من يريد الدنيا بعمل الآخرة ، كالمنافق ، والمرائي ، والمهاجر للدنيا ، والمجاهد للغنيمة والذكر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r8.claim: A prophetic report says migration is valued according to its aim: migration to God and His Messenger is for them, while migration for a worldly prize is only for that prize.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r8.anchor: كما قال صلى الله عليه وسلم . ( 606 ) ( فمن كانت هجرته إلى الله ورسوله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p613#2/r9.claim: Madḥūr means expelled from God's mercy.

FARRA:v2p119/r9.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p119/r9.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p119/r9.claim: عجلنا له فيها ما نشاء لمن نريد means that God gives from this-worldly provision to whomever He chooses.

MUQATIL:17:16-18/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:17:16-18/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:17:16-18/r3.claim: Whoever wants immediate worldly life receives whatever wealth God wills for whomever He chooses, then is sent to Hell, blamed by God and driven away.
MUQATIL:17:16-18/r3.anchor: { من كان يريد } في الدنيا، { العاجلة عجلنا له فيها } ، يعني في الدنيا، { ما نشآء لمن نريد } ، من المال، { ثم جعلنا له جهنم }

MUQATIL:17:16-18/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:17:16-18/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:17:16-18/r4.claim: The passage is said to have been revealed about three men from Thaqif, naming Farqad ibn Yamama, Abu Fatima ibn al-Bukhturi, and Safwan; the source then adds two unnamed placeholders.
MUQATIL:17:16-18/r4.anchor: نزلت في ثلاثة نفر من ثقيف، فى: فرقد بن يمامة، وأبي فاطمة بن البحتري، وصفوان، وفلان، وفلان.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p282/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p282/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p282/r1.claim: The phrase for whom We wish is a partitive apposition to the preceding phrase, repeating its preposition; its pronoun refers to the person seeking this life.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p282/r1.anchor: بدل من له بإعادة الجار وهو بدل البعض من الكل إذ الضمير يرجع إلى من

NASAFI-FULL:v2p282/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p282/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p282/r2.claim: God controls both what worldly benefit is accelerated and which seeker receives it; people may desire more than they receive, or be denied even what others obtain.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p282/r2.anchor: فقيد المعجل بمشيئته والمعجل له بإرادته وهكذا الحال ترى كثيرا من هؤلاء يتمنون ما يتمنون ولا يعطون إلا بعضا منه

NASAFI-FULL:v2p282/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p282/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p282/r3.claim: The pious believer chooses the wealth of the afterlife; worldly poverty may be better for that believer than receiving a worldly share.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p282/r3.anchor: وأما المؤمن التقى فقد اختار غنى الآخرة فإن أوتى حظا من الدنيا فبها وإلا فربما كان الفقر خيرا له

NASAFI-FULL:v2p282/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p282/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p282/r4.claim: The worldly seeker enters Hell in the afterlife, despised and expelled from God's mercy.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p282/r4.anchor: ممقوتا ﴿ مدحورا ﴾ مطرودا من رحمة الله

QURTUBI-FULL:17:18-19/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:18-19/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:18-19/r1.claim: The worldly seeker receives only what God wills, then faces accountability and Hell; hypocrites and show-offs who feign devotion for spoils gain no afterlife reward and receive only their allotted worldly share.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:18-19/r1.anchor: أي لم نعطه منها إلا ما نشاء ثم نؤاخذه بعمله، وعاقبته دخول النار.

QURTUBI-FULL:17:18-19/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:18-19/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:18-19/r2.claim: The wording refers to the immediate abode by its adjective; “rejected and banished” describes removal from God’s mercy.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:18-19/r2.anchor: يعني الدنيا، والمراد الدار العاجلة فعبر بالنعت عن المنعوت.

MAJAZ:v1p374/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p374/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p374/r2.claim: مدحورا means expelled and removed; أدحر الشيطان means repel Satan, and the verbal noun is الدحور.
MAJAZ:v1p374/r2.anchor: «مدحورا» (18) أي مقصى مبعدا، يقال: أدحر الشيطان عنك، [ومصدره الدحور]

RAZI-FULL:v20p142#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p142#2/r1.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v20p142#2/r1.claim: Al-Qaffal connects this verse to each person’s assigned “bird”: those seeking only worldly status may reject the prophets, yet receive only what God wills and end in Hell.
RAZI-FULL:v20p142#2/r1.anchor: قال القفال رحمه الله : هذه الآية داخلة في معنى قوله : { وكل إنسان ألزمناه طئره فى عنقه }

RAZI-FULL:v20p142#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p142#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p142#2/r2.claim: Hell’s wording depicts punishment as lasting harm with humiliation and exile from divine mercy, without relief or escape.
RAZI-FULL:v20p142#2/r2.anchor: العقاب عبارة عن مضرة مقرونة بالإهانة والذم بشرط أن تكون دائمة

RAZI-FULL:v20p142#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p142#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p142#2/r3.claim: Worldly success should not be mistaken for God’s approval: it may end in punishment, and a person’s deeds can drive them like an ill omen toward torment.
RAZI-FULL:v20p142#2/r3.anchor: مساعدة الدنيا لا ينبغي أن يستدل بها على رضا الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v20p142#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p142#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p142#2/r4.claim: The phrase “for whom We will” warns that many who abandon religion for worldly gain obtain neither; they are the greatest losers despite thinking they act well.
RAZI-FULL:v20p142#2/r4.anchor: يدل على أنه لا يحصل الفوز بالدنيا لكل أحد

RAZI-FULL:v20p144/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p144/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p144/r6.claim: He classifies actions by whether they aim at worldly good, afterlife good, both together, or neither; the verse directly treats the first two.
RAZI-FULL:v20p144/r6.anchor: فإما أن يقصد بذلك الفعل تحصيل خيرات الدنيا

NAHHAS:v2p419/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p419/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p419/r13.claim: God does not withhold the immediate world from one who does not seek the afterlife’s reward; He grants it to whom He wills.
NAHHAS:v2p419/r13.anchor: أي لا يريد ثوابا في الآخرة لم نمنعه ذلك ^ ( لمن نريد ) ^

STUDYQURAN:17:18/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:18/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:17:18/r1.claim: Those seeking only worldly goods while denying or despairing of the Hereafter may receive what they want here, subject to God’s will, and then face Hell.
STUDYQURAN:17:18/r1.anchor: God may hasten for them precisely what they desire; that is, He may grant them worldly goods in the here and now, but with the caveat whatsoever We will for whomsoever We desire

STUDYQURAN:17:18/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:18/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:17:18/r4.claim: Those desiring the ephemeral may include people performing apparently pious acts hypocritically or only for worldly gain.
STUDYQURAN:17:18/r4.anchor: Those who desire the ephemeral in v. 18 may include not only those whose worldly desires lead them to outwardly sinful behavior

TAB-FULL:v14p535#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p535#3/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p535#3/r1.claim: The worldly seeker works only for immediate life and lacks belief in resurrection or hope of divine reward or punishment; God gives such a person whatever worldly ease, hardship, or chastisement He wills, to whomever He wills.
TAB-FULL:v14p535#3/r1.anchor: من كان طلبه الدنيا العاجلة ولها يعمل ويسعى، وإياها يبتغي، لا يوقن بمعاد ولا يرجو ثوابا

TAB-FULL:v14p535#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p535#3/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p535#3/r2.claim: At the resurrection God sends this person to Hell, blamed for ingratitude and bad conduct toward prior favors and expelled far away.
TAB-FULL:v14p535#3/r2.anchor: على قلة شكره إيانا وسوء صنيعه فيما سلف من أيادينا عنده في الدنيا

TAB-FULL:v14p535#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p535#3/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v14p535#3/r3.claim: Qatāda describes worldly life as the person's sole concern, aim, and intention, followed by being driven into Hell; the person is blamed amid God's favor and cast away amid His punishment.
TAB-FULL:v14p535#3/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {من كان يريد العاجلة عجلنا له فيها ما نشاء لمن نريد} [الإسراء: 18] يقول: من كانت الدنيا همه

TAB-FULL:v14p535#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p535#3/r4.speaker: أبو إسحاق الفزاري
TAB-FULL:v14p535#3/r4.claim: Abū Isḥāq explains “for whom We will” as meaning someone whose destruction God wills.
TAB-FULL:v14p535#3/r4.anchor: ثني أبو طيبة شيخ من أهل المصيصة، أنه سمع أبا إسحاق الفزاري، يقول: {عجلنا له فيها ما نشاء لمن نريد} [الإسراء: 18] قال: لمن نريد هلكته

TAB-FULL:v14p535#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p535#3/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v14p535#3/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses مذموما as blameworthy or reproached.
TAB-FULL:v14p535#3/r5.anchor: عن علي، عن ابن عباس، قوله {مذموما} [الإسراء: 18] يقول: ملوما

TAB-FULL:v14p535#3/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p535#3/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v14p535#3/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd explains العاجلة as the present world.
TAB-FULL:v14p535#3/r6.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {من كان يريد العاجلة عجلنا له فيها ما نشاء لمن نريد} [الإسراء: 18] قال: العاجلة: الدنيا

TABATABAI:17:9-22#14/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#14/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#14/r2.claim: Al-ʿājila is an omitted noun's adjective, probably worldly life because it contrasts with the afterlife next; others say it means immediate blessings or transient worldly goods.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#14/r2.anchor: العاجلة صفة محذوفة الموصوف ولعل موصوفها الحياة بقرينة مقابلتها للآخرة

TABATABAI:17:9-22#14/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#14/r3.speaker: المفردات
TABATABAI:17:9-22#14/r3.claim: The lexicon explains ṣaly as kindling or enduring the heat of fire, while ṣallā can mean entering it and aṣlā can mean causing someone to enter it.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#14/r3.anchor: وفي المفردات أصل الصلي لإيقاد النار. قال وقال الخليل صلى الكافر النار قاسى حرها

TABATABAI:17:9-22#14/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#14/r4.speaker: المجمع
TABATABAI:17:9-22#14/r4.claim: The lexicon defines being driven away as expulsion and distance.

TABATABAI:17:9-22#14/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#14/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#14/r5.claim: After discussing worldly destruction following a prophetic mission, the passage turns to afterlife punishment, reward, and the general principle governing both.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#14/r5.anchor: عاد إلى بيان سنته في التعذيب الأخروي والإثابة فيها في هذه الآية والآيتين بعدها

TABATABAI:17:9-22#14/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#14/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#14/r6.claim: Wanting worldly life means seeking its pleasures as an independent end; using the world as a route to afterlife happiness is itself pursuit of the afterlife.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#14/r6.anchor: إنما يعد طلبا لها إذا كانت مقصودة بالاستقلال لا لأجل التوسل بها إلى سعادة الأخرى

TABATABAI:17:9-22#14/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#14/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#14/r7.claim: The continuing expression من كان يريد describes someone persistently devoted to this material life, neglecting the afterlife and thereby emptying belief and religion of purpose.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#14/r7.anchor: حيث يدل على استمرار الإرادة. وهذا هو الذي لا يرى لنفسه إلا هذه الحياة المادية الدنيوية

TABATABAI:17:9-22#15/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#15/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#15/r1.claim: God hastens to the worldly seeker only what He chooses, for whom He chooses; human desire does not govern divine allocation.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#15/r1.anchor: لكن لا بإعطائه ما يريده بل بإعطائه ما نريده فالأمر إلينا لا إليه

TABATABAI:17:9-22#15/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#15/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#15/r2.claim: Worldly seekers receive what the surrounding causes permit; their requests by the language of their condition yield only what those causes lead to.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#15/r2.anchor: يرزق منها على حسب ما تسمح له الأسباب والعوامل التي أجراها الله في الكون

TABATABAI:17:9-22#15/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#15/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#15/r3.claim: A passage about silver roofs for disbelievers shows that worldly wealth follows the shared causal order and has no value in the afterlife's scale.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#15/r3.anchor: ولا فرق بين الكافر والمؤمن قبال العلل الكونية بل من صادفته أسباب الغنى والثروة أثرته وأغنته

TABATABAI:17:9-22#15/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#15/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#15/r4.claim: The reading that one wants the world specifically through one's deeds is an unsupported restriction drawn from Hud; that passage concerns recompense for deeds, while this passage contrasts life-goals.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#15/r4.anchor: وهو تقييد من غير مقيد، ولعله أخذه من قوله تعالى

TABATABAI:17:9-22#16/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#16/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#16/r1.claim: The worldly seeker is made to enter Hell, disgraced and expelled from mercy; these descriptions indicate exclusion from forgiveness and mercy.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#16/r1.anchor: والقيدان يفيدان أنه مخصوص بجهنم محروم من المغفرة والرحمة

TABATABAI:17:9-22#16/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#16/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#16/r2.claim: Attachment to this world and denial of the next have degrees: some show them in both word and deed, others in deed while verbally acknowledging the afterlife.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#16/r2.anchor: فمن ذلك ما هو كذلك قولا وفعلا ومنه ما هو كذلك فعلا مع الاعتراف به قولا

TABATABAI:17:9-22#17/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#17/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#17/r1.claim: Afterlife-directed deeds reliably reach their ends, unlike worldly causes, since God says the effort is thanked but worldly provision is only what He wills for whom He wills.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#17/r1.anchor: وفي الآيتين دلالة على أن الأسباب الأخروية وهي الأعمال لا تتخلف عن غاياتها بخلاف الأسباب الدنيوية

TABATABAI:17:9-22#18/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#18/r7.speaker: روح المعاني
TABATABAI:17:9-22#18/r7.claim: A reported taxonomy divides agents into those seeking this world, the afterlife, both, or neither; mixed motives then divide according to which desire predominates or whether they are equal.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#18/r7.anchor: والتقسيم الحاصر أن كل فاعل إما أن يريد بفعله العاجلة فقط أو يريد الآخرة فقط أو يريدهما معا

TABATABAI:17:9-22#18/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#18/r8.speaker: روح المعاني
TABATABAI:17:9-22#18/r8.claim: The reported discussion says scholars disagree over accepting mixed-motive deeds when afterlife intent predominates, but agree against deeds where worldly motive predominates or ties.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#18/r8.anchor: ونقل اختلاف العلماء في قبول هذا النوع من العمل، ونقل اتفاقهم على عدم قبول ما يترجح فيه باعث الدنيا

TABATABAI:17:9-22#19/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#19/r1.speaker: روح المعاني
TABATABAI:17:9-22#19/r1.claim: The fourth type is impossible for those who require every voluntary act to have a motive; others say such an act has no inner effect but remains outwardly forbidden.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#19/r1.anchor: وأما القسم الرابع عند القائلين بأن صدور الفعل من القادر يتوقف على حصول الداعي فهو ممتنع الحصول

TABATABAI:17:9-22#19/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#19/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#19/r2.claim: These verses classify a person's ultimate life-goal, not the acceptance of every individual act: seeking this world treats it as the end, while seeking the afterlife treats this world as a stage toward it.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#19/r2.anchor: أن الآيات الكريمة ليست في مقام بيان حكم الرد والقبول بالنسبة إلى كل عمل صدر عن عامل

TABRISI:17:18/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:18/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:18/r2.claim: Yuslīhā is circumstantial, and 'for whom We will' apposes the preceding clause; the pronoun repeats because the apposition is another clause.
TABRISI:17:18/r2.anchor: ويصليها في موضع نصب على الحال لمن نريد بدل من قوله: { عجلنا له فيها ما نشاء }

TABRISI:17:18#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:18#2/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:18#2/r10.claim: The immediate world is named for its short-lived quality; God grants only what He wills to whom He wills and may restrict the worldly seeker.
TABRISI:17:18#2/r10.anchor: أي النعم العاجلة وهي الدنيا فعبر عنها بصفتها { عجلنا له فيها ما نشاء }

TABRISI:17:18#2/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:18#2/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:18#2/r11.claim: The worldly seeker enters Hell blamed and excluded from God's mercy.
TABRISI:17:18#2/r11.anchor: { مذموما } ملوما { مدحورا } مبعدا من رحمة الله

TABRISI:17:19-22/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:19-22/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:19-22/r1.claim: Work done for worldly reward alone, without seeking God or the hereafter, earns only the worldly portion God wills and no afterlife reward; the gift may be misused and punished.
TABRISI:17:19-22/r1.anchor: معنى الآية من كان يريد ثواب الدنيا بعمله الذي افترضه الله عليه لا يريد به وجه الله

THALABI:v6p91/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p91/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p91/r6.claim: The urgent life means this world; the adjective stands for “the urgent abode.” God grants only what He wills to whom He wills, whether abundance or restriction.
THALABI:v6p91/r6.anchor: من كان يريد العاجلة يعني الدنيا فعبرنا بحرف عن الاسم

THALABI:v6p91/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p91/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p91/r7.claim: The worldly seeker eventually enters Hell, disgraced and expelled.
THALABI:v6p91/r7.anchor: ثم جعلنا له جهنم في الآخرة يصلاها يدخلها مذموما مدحورا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p292/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p292/r1.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p292/r1.claim: Al-ʿājila is the present world, contrasted with the delayed Hereafter; worldly seekers receive only the amount God chooses for whom He chooses, not whatever they desire.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p292/r1.anchor: قال المفسرون: أى الدنيا (¬2)، والعاجلة نقيض الآجلة؛ وهي الدنيا عجلت وكانت قبل الآخرة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p292/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p292/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p292/r2.claim: This rebukes those who serve or profess Islam for worldly gain: many seeking it may fail, and whoever gets it receives only a divine allotment before entering Hell.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p292/r2.anchor: هذا ذم لمن أراد بعمله وطاعته وإسلامه الدنيا ومنفعتها وعروضها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p292/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p292/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p292/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses mazmūm as blameworthy and madḥūr as expelled or driven away.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p292/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ملوما (¬5)، {مدحورا}: منفيا مطرودا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p292#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p292#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p292#2/r1.claim: The verse parallels 3:145 about receiving a share of worldly reward.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p292#2/r1.anchor: ومعنى هذه الآية كقوله: {ومن يرد ثواب الدنيا نؤته منها}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p292#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p292#2/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p292#2/r2.claim: Abū Isḥāq says such a person is put in Hell because he did not seek God through his deeds; madḥūr also means removed from God's mercy.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p292#2/r2.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: {ثم جعلنا له جهنم}؛ لأنه لم يرد الله بعمله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:18-22/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:18-22/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:18-22/r1.claim: One who seeks worldly life through deeds, worship, or Islam receives only the amount God wills, and only for whom He wills.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:18-22/r1.anchor: { من كان يريد العاجلة } بعمله وطاعته وإسلامه الدنيا { عجلنا له فيها ما نشاء } القدر الذي نشاء { لمن نريد }

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:18-22/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:18-22/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:18-22/r2.claim: Such a person enters Hell in the afterlife, blamed and banished for not intending God through his deeds.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:18-22/r2.anchor: ثم يدخل النار في الآخرة { مذموما } ملوما { مدحورا } مطرودا لأنه لم يرد الله سبحانه بعمله.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p123/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p123/r8.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p123/r8.claim: The one seeking only the immediate world is the idolater who does not believe in the Hereafter.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p123/r8.anchor: قوله: {من كان يريد العاجلة} [الإسراء: 18] وهذا المشرك الذي لا يريد إلا الدنيا، لا يؤمن بالآخرة.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p124/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p124/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p124/r1.claim: The one who receives what God wills of worldly benefit will still enter Hell amid God’s punishment.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p124/r1.anchor: {عجلنا له فيها ما نشاء لمن نريد ثم جعلنا له جهنم يصلاها مذموما} [الإسراء: 18] في نقمة الله.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p124/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p124/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p124/r2.claim: To be driven away means being banished far from Paradise and placed in Hell.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p124/r2.anchor: {مدحورا} [الإسراء: 18] مطرودا، مباعدا عن الجنة، في النار.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p124/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p124/r3.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p124/r3.claim: Qatāda glosses “blamed” as being in God’s punishment and “banished” as being in His torment.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p124/r3.anchor: سعيد، عن قتادة، قال: مذموما في نقمة الله، مدحورا في عذاب الله.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p124/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p124/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p124/r4.claim: For one whose concern and pursuit are only worldly life, God hastens what He wills for whom He wills, then assigns Hell.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p124/r4.anchor: يقول: من كانت الدنيا همه وطلبته {عجلنا له فيها ما نشاء لمن نريد ثم جعلنا له جهنم} [الإسراء: 18]

SAMIN-DURR:17:18/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:18/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:18/r1.claim: من is conditional, عجلنا its answer, ما يشاء its object, and لمن نريد a partitive apposition from له with the governor repeated.
SAMIN-DURR:17:18/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { من كان }: " من " شرطية، و " عجلنا " جوابه، و " ما يشاء " مفعوله

SAMIN-DURR:17:18/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:18/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:18/r2.claim: جعل is causative here; يصلاها is circumstantial from either له or جهنم, and مذموما is circumstantial from the subject of يصلاها.
SAMIN-DURR:17:18/r2.anchor: قوله: " يصلاها " الجملة حال: إما من الضمير في " له " وإما من " جهنم " ، و " مذموما " حال من فاعل

SAMIN-DURR:17:18/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:18/r3.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:17:18/r3.claim: An omitted contrasting condition is understood: the one who wants the immediate life also strives for it while being an unbeliever, as the following context indicates.
SAMIN-DURR:17:18/r3.anchor: قيل: وفي الكلام حذف، وهو حذف المقابل؛ إذ الأصل: من كان يريد العاجلة وسعى لها سعيها وهو كافر

SAMIN-DURR:17:18/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:18/r4.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:17:18/r4.claim: Alternatively, the intended person wants worldly life through deeds directed toward the Hereafter, like a hypocrite.
SAMIN-DURR:17:18/r4.anchor: وقيل: بل الأصل: من كان يريد العاجلة بعمله للآخرة كالمنافق.

ELMALILI:17:18/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:18/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:18/r1.claim: Seeking the immediate life means working for the world and demanding one’s wages before death; God grants in this world only what He wills, to whom He wills, not necessarily the amount each person asks.
ELMALILI:17:18/r1.anchor: dünya için çalışır, amelinin ecrini ölmeden bu hayât-ı dünyada almak isterse

ELMALILI:17:18/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:18/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:18/r2.claim: The value of a deed is determined by the one who employs and accepts it, not by the worker’s request; nevertheless Hud 11:15 promises full payment for their works with no one shortchanged.
ELMALILI:17:18/r2.anchor: çalışanın istediği ile değil, çalıştıranın kabulü ile ta‘ayyün eder.

ELMALILI:17:18/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:18/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:18/r3.claim: Immediate worldly preference may look pleasant at first, but its outcome is Hell, where the person is disgraced and expelled.
ELMALILI:17:18/r3.anchor: işte acûl olmanın önü hoş gibi görünürse de âkıbeti böyle vahimdir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:18/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:18/r1.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:18/r1.claim: Razi reads verse 18 as explaining verse 13's personal responsibility: one who chooses worldly gain is in a test, receives only what God wills, and merits blame and Hell by pursuing worldly desire over God's pleasure.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:18/r1.anchor: Râzî’nin kaydettiği bir yoruma göre 18. âyet 13. âyetin

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:18/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:18/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:18/r2.claim: Worldly advantages are not true superiority; seeking the hereafter concerns one's aim, not merely the type of work, since worldly tasks can serve the hereafter and worship can serve worldly gain.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:18/r2.anchor: burada yapılan iş değil, o işle neyin hedeflendiğinin altı çizilmekte, yani niyetlere dikkat çekilmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:18/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:18/r3.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:18/r3.claim: The Prophet teaches that deeds are judged according to intentions.

ZAJJAJ:v3p233/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p233/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p233/r2.claim: العاجلة means this world; God hastens to a person who seeks it only what God wills, for whomever God wills, not whatever the person wills.
ZAJJAJ:v3p233/r2.anchor: أي من كان يريد العاجلة بعمله، أي الدنيا، عجل الله لمن أراد أن يعجل له مايشاء الله

ZAJJAJ:v3p233/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p233/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p233/r3.claim: Alternatively, the implied subject of نشاء is the servant: God gives the servant what he desires, if God wills it.
ZAJJAJ:v3p233/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المضمر في نشاء " من "، المعنى عجلنا للعبد ما يشتهيه

ZAJJAJ:v3p233/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p233/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p233/r4.claim: The threat of Hell follows because the person did not intend God through his deed.
ZAJJAJ:v3p233/r4.anchor: ثم جعلنا له جهنم). لأنه لم يرد الله بعمله

ZAJJAJ:v3p233/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p233/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p233/r5.claim: مذموما and مذءوما have the same meaning.

ZAJJAJ:v3p233/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p233/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p233/r6.claim: مدحورا means driven far away from God's mercy; دحر means to drive someone away.
ZAJJAJ:v3p233/r6.anchor: أي مباعدا من رحمة الله. يقال: دحرته أدحره دحرا ودحورا

ASAD-NOTES:17:18#n23/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:17:18#n23/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:17:18#n23/r1.claim: The phrase literally means assigning hell to a person.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p27/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p27/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p27/r10.claim: The عاجلة is worldly life, and wanting it means preferring it over the afterlife; the omitted counterpart is that the worldly seeker acts for it while faith is absent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p27/r10.anchor: والعاجلة هي الدنيا ومعنى إرادتها إيثارها على الآخرة، ولا بد من تقدير حذف دل عليه المقابل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p27/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p27/r11.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p27/r11.claim: Another view concerns people who use afterlife deeds for worldly gain, such as hypocrites, show-offs, migrants seeking worldly benefit, or fighters seeking booty and renown.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p27/r11.anchor: وقيل: المراد من كان يريد العاجلة بعمل الآخرة كالمنافق والمرائي والمهاجر للدنيا والمجاهد للغنيمة والذكر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p27/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p27/r12.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p27/r12.claim: The Prophetic report says that whoever migrates for a worldly prize or a woman has only the worldly object for which he migrated.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p27/r12.anchor: ومن كانت هجرته إلى دنيا يصيبها أو امرأة ينكحها فهجرته إلى ما هاجر إليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p27/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p27/r13.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p27/r13.claim: A report warns that whoever seeks worldly gain through afterlife deeds receives no share in the afterlife.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p27/r13.anchor: من طلب الدنيا بعمل الآخرة فما له في الآخرة من نصيب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p27/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p27/r14.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p27/r14.claim: A reported occasion of revelation is hypocrites joining Muslim campaigns for booty rather than reward.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p27/r14.anchor: وقيل: نزلت في المنافقين وكانوا يغزون مع المسلمين للغنيمة لا للثواب،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p27/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p27/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p27/r15.claim: The conditional promise is limited twice: God hastens only what He wills and only for whom He wills, so worldly seekers do not necessarily obtain their wishes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p27/r15.anchor: عجلنا له فيها ما نشاء فقيد المعجل بمشيئته أي ما يشاء تعجيله. ولمن نريد بدل من قوله: له

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p27/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p27/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p27/r16.claim: The majority read ما نشاء with first-person plural; a report from Nāfiʿ reads يشاء in third person, either as a shift referring to God or as referring to the conditional seeker, though not universally.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p27/r16.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور ما نشاء بالنون وروي عن نافع ما يشاء بالياء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p27/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p27/r17.speaker: أبو إسحاق الفزاري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p27/r17.claim: Al-Fazārī interprets لمن نريد as one whom God intends to destroy, but Abū Ḥayyān says the wording does not support this.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p27/r17.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق الفزاري المعنى لمن نريد هلكته وما قاله لا يدل عليه لفظ في الآية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p28/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p28/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p28/r1.claim: جعلنا means made: Hell is the first object and its second complement is implied by the construction, yielding Hell as the unbelievers’ destination; another grammarian supplies an omitted second object meaning destination or recompense.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p28/r1.anchor: وجعلنا بمعنى صيرنا، والمفعول الأول جهنم والثاني له لأنه ينعقد منهما مبتدأ وخبر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p28/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p28/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p28/r2.claim: مذموما signals humiliation, while مدحورا signals distance and expulsion from God’s mercy.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p28/r2.anchor: مذموما إشارة إلى الإهانة. مدحورا إشارة إلى البعد والطرد من رحمة الله

NASHR:v1p290/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p290/r1.speaker: عامة أهل الأداء
NASHR:v1p290/r1.claim: Most performance authorities assimilate the adjacent sounds in this locus; this is the practice across Ibn Farḥ’s routes from al-Dūrī and Ibn Jarīr’s routes from al-Sūsī and was read by al-Dānī and his students.
NASHR:v1p290/r1.anchor: فروى إدغامه عامة أهل الأداء، وهو الذي عليه جميع طرق ابن فرح

NASHR:v1p290/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p290/r2.speaker: جميع العراقيين
NASHR:v1p290/r2.claim: All Iraqi transmitters use izhār through every route of Abū al-Zarʿāʾ from al-Dūrī and every route of al-Sūsī; the author accepts both assimilation and izhār.
NASHR:v1p290/r2.anchor: وروى إظهاره جميع العراقيين، عن جميع طرق أبي الزعراء عن الدوري

NASHR:v1p290/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p290/r5.speaker: القاسم بن عبد الوارث وصاحب التجريد
NASHR:v1p290/r5.claim: Al-Dūrī via al-Qāsim ibn ʿAbd al-Wārith transmits assimilation in فلا جناح عليه, المسيح عيسى, and الريح عاصفة; al-Tajrīd reports it from Shuʿja and ʿUbayd Allāh in فلا جناح and المسيح.
NASHR:v1p290/r5.anchor: وقد روى القاسم بن عبد الوارث عن الدوري إدغام فلا جناح عليه

NASHR:v1p290/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p290/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p290/r6.claim: Izhār is sounder and the working practice; consensus on keeping even a static ḥāʾ clear in فاصفح عنهم shows that ḥāʾ-to-ʿayn assimilation is transmitted only, not analogical.

NASHR:v1p290/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p290/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p290/r7.claim: Dāl assimilates into ten following letters regardless of its vowel, except an open dāl preceded by a consonant assimilates only into tāʾ; dāl into tāʾ assimilates in every case because the letters share an articulation point.
NASHR:v1p290/r7.anchor: والدال تدغم في عشرة أحرف: التاء، والثاء، والجيم

NASHR:v1p290/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p290/r8.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p290/r8.claim: Reports of izhār for dāl before tāʾ or jīm arise from meeting two sukūns; the author says the real difference is concealment versus assimilation, following the experts and preferring the view supported by the strength of kasra.
NASHR:v1p290/r8.anchor: والصحيح أن الخلاف في ذلك هو في الإخفاء والإدغام من كون الساكن قبله حرفا صحيحا كما سيأتي التنبيه عليه آخر الباب

BURHAN:v2p16/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p16/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p16/r1.claim: When people who pursue the world receive little, the answer is that God grants the immediate world only as much as He wills and to whom He wills.

ITQAN:v2p432/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p432/r1.speaker: الأخفش
ITQAN:v2p432/r1.claim: Al-Akhfash parses idha in 17:18 as governed in the genitive by hatta.
ITQAN:v2p432/r1.anchor: قال الأخفش في قوله تعالى ﴿ حتى إذا جاؤوها ﴾ إن إذا جر بحتى

ITQAN:v2p432/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p432/r3.speaker: الجمهور
ITQAN:v2p432/r3.claim: Most grammarians reject taking idha outside its adverbial role: hatta begins the full clause, the second idha apposes the first, and the first has an omitted response inferred as the people dividing into three groups.
ITQAN:v2p432/r3.anchor: والجمهور أنكروا خروجها عن الظرفية وقالوا في الآية الأولى إن حتى حرف ابتداء داخل على الجملة بأسرها

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p41/r10.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p41/r10.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p41/r10.claim: The codex writes ما نشؤا with wāw after alif in Shuʿayb's verse, while the same form elsewhere lacks wāw, without a difference in meaning.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p41/r10.anchor: بواو بعد الألف، وفي موضع آخر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p592/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p592/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p592/r2.claim: In conditional clauses, he uses the present for actions expected to recur and the past for actions that do not or should not recur; examples include repeated gratitude versus one-time disbelief and accidental versus deliberate killing.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p592/r2.anchor: استعمال فعل المضارع مع الشرط يكون إذا كان مضمون أن يتكرر.
